title: River Flows in You
credit: Simple MidiMan arrangement of the Yiruma piece, from Ishay’s sheet — a first real song, not a full transcription
_notation: Per hand, one string per bar. Tokens: pitch (G4, Bb3, C#5), chord [G4 Bb4 D5], rest r. Suffix :n = length in eighths (default 1; fractions like 1/2 allowed). Prefix ~ = tied from the previous token of the same pitch (no new attack). Prefix / = rolled chord. This song is 6/8: every bar must sum to 6 eighths. The beat is the dotted quarter (two beats a bar).

sections.name: Intro
sections.hint: Left hand alone: A minor, F, C, G — root, fifth, octave, twice each bar. Two dotted-quarter beats. Right hand waits.
sections.coach: Four bars of the A minor arpeggio — A, F, C, G. That’s the whole song.

sections.name: Theme
sections.hint: The tune everyone knows. Right hand is A–G♯–A–B into a held A; left hand keeps the same four-chord arpeggio. Bars 27–28 are the written 1st and 2nd endings, played through once.
sections.coach: The tune — A, G sharp, A, B — over the same four chords.

sections.name: Theme 2
sections.hint: Same river, a few more sixteenths in the right hand. Keep the left hand even; don’t chase the ornaments.
sections.coach: Same river, a few more sixteenths. Keep the left hand even.

sections.name: Outro
sections.hint: The arpeggio stops. Left hand holds a dotted half each bar; right hand steps down to the last A minor chord.
sections.coach: Long notes now. End on A minor.
